contract_findings: SCOPE of this list: every item is read from the bytes and proved PER CALL (one successful call implies ...). No item is a theorem over a sequence of calls, and nothing here reads the live chain state (who holds a role today is not known to the proofs).
mint(usr, wad): only wards[caller] == 1. A ward mints any amount to any address; the only checks are the overflow of balanceOf[usr] and of totalSupply. No cap, no zero-address check.
rely(usr) / deny(usr): only wards[caller] == 1; they write wards[usr] = 1 / 0. A ward can add or remove any ward, itself included.
burn(usr, wad): no ward needed. The caller is usr, or has allowance[usr][caller] >= wad (an allowance of 2^256-1 is not reduced). balanceOf[usr] and totalSupply go down by wad.
transferFrom / move / pull / push: DAI style; an allowance of 2^256-1 is not reduced; no zero-address checks.

permit: DAI style (holder, spender, nonce, expiry, allowed, v, r, s). Check order in the bytes: holder != 0, ecrecover == holder, expiry == 0 or now <= expiry, nonce == nonces[holder]; then nonces[holder] + 1 and allowance[holder][spender] = 0 or 2^256-1. The domain separator is the word of storage slot 5 (set at construction, not recomputed with CHAINID). v is masked to its low byte before the call.
Every function reverts on a nonzero value. name, symbol, version write nothing and log nothing.

reuse_notes.all: The call model is in TokenKit/Evm/Precompile.lean: ecrecover_call_ok takes the frame at GAS, the bytes of GAS STATICCALL and of the 16-byte revert-bubble idiom of solc (ISZERO DUP1 ISZERO PUSH2 JUMPI RETURNDATASIZE PUSH1 0 DUP1 RETURNDATACOPY RETURNDATASIZE PUSH1 0 REVERT) and gives the frame after the call with EthLib's compute in memory. Per token: config prefix_functions + stops at the GAS pc, one segment from the pc after STATICCALL with raw_mem + post_def, then a hand file like Usdd/Permit.lean (digest_bytes, permit_call, ok_permit_real; about 250 lines, mostly statement).
reuse_notes.DAI: solc 0.5.12, optimizer off: same DAI-style permit and storage, but the call sequence differs (the unoptimized code pushes gas with GAS then SUB or a literal, and checks with ISZERO ISZERO before the bubble). ecrecover_call_ok fixes the 16 idiom bytes and gas = GAS; a variant with the 0.5 byte pattern is needed (staticcall_outcome, ecrecover_ran and incorporateChild_precompile are reused as they are). Memory is aligned in 0.5 unoptimized code only up to abi.encodePacked of 0x1901: raw_words is still needed. DOMAIN_SEPARATOR is in storage as here.
reuse_notes.SKY: solc 0.8 with PUSH0 (from Shanghai): needs PUSH0 in the generator rules (bubble idiom uses PUSH0 instead of PUSH1 0: a second idiom lemma next to bubble_no_ok), EIP-2612 permit (owner, spender, value, deadline, v, r, s) with the domain separator rebuilt from CHAINID and ADDRESS when the chain id changed (CHAINID and ADDRESS rules, a branch), and an ERC-1271 path: when the signer has code the contract STATICCALLs it (isValidSignature). That call is to arbitrary code and can not be closed with the precompile model; state it with the result of the child run as a parameter or exclude that branch in a listed way.
reuse_notes.USDE_ENA: OpenZeppelin ERC20Permit, solc 0.8 with PUSH0: ECDSA.recover checks s <= n/2 and v in {27, 28} before the call and reverts with custom errors; _domainSeparatorV4 compares CHAINID and ADDRESS with immutables in the code (cached separator in code, not storage). Needs PUSH0, CHAINID, ADDRESS rules, the PUSH0 bubble idiom, nonces via a Counters mapping, and permitStruct with value instead of allowed. The STATICCALL lemmas are reused; the fork lower bound becomes Shanghai.

fork_range.headline: Every claim of this file is for Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam (transactions: Dencun <= fork < Glamsterdam). Nothing is claimed for Glamsterdam or later.
fork_range.why: The proofs use the one-counter gas meter (Evm fork Nat). EthLib runs that meter only before Glamsterdam; from Glamsterdam it runs the two-counter meter of EIP-8037, which is not ported.
fork_range.stated_in_the_theorem: fork < .glamsterdam is a hypothesis of: ok_permit_real, permit_readable, supply_permit, process_step_all, process_step_all_inv, permitCall_process, callsP_process, frameKeepsR, supply_message_any_depth, supply_transaction, supply_any_transactions, supply_from_zero (Tx.lean), and of every theorem of Instance.lean and PermitRun.lean that is about a run (supply_m0, ecrecover_call_runs, permit_runs, supply_permit_m1, permit_runs_inv).
fork_range.not_stated_in_the_theorem: The older generated theorems (block rules, path specs, ok_<fn>, supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, <fn>_readable, the Sanity witnesses) and the hand-written older per-message model of Seq.lean (process_step, process_step_inv, calls_process) carry only the lower bound (Berlin <= fork; Seq.lean from Paris). They are statements about the one-counter model and are true as stated at every such fork, but they describe what EthLib really runs only before Glamsterdam. The bound was NOT added to them: it would have to come from the generators in token-kit/scripts (shared by every token, outside the scope of this fix round), and adding a hypothesis that the proofs do not use would change no proof. Read each of them with fork < Glamsterdam; every headline that reaches a message or a transaction (the lists above) states it.

closed_instance.audit: the ten-token audit, fix 5 (USDD-3): PARTLY closed
closed_instance.plain_answer: There is NO closed instance of Sep, and so no theorem under Sep (supply_<fn>, supply_preserved, supply_permit, the readable theorems of the writers, the sequence and transaction theorems) has an instance with every hypothesis proved. Each open fact of Sep says that a given slot is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a: a statement over 2^160 values of keccak. keccak is a real function here, but no proof can run it 2^160 times and no shorter argument is known (it is preimage and collision resistance). Under the usual random-function view each fact fails with chance about 2^-96.
closed_instance.state_and_call: state sState C []: one account at the contract C, every storage word 0. Call m0: allowance(K, K) sent by HOLDER, the address with the word K = 0x19e7e376e7c213b7e7e7e46cc70a5dd086daff2a (the address of the public test key 0x11...11), so the three mapping keys of the call are K, K, K.
proved_with_no_hypothesis: inv_start: the start invariant Inv holds in that state (sum of balances 0, total supply 0)
callKeys_m0, callKeys_m1: the keys of the two calls are [K, K, K]
computed by the kernel with the real keccak: allow_ne_total, nonce_ne_total, allow_ne_nonce, ward_ne_total
sep_iff, sep_m0_iff: Sep [K, K, K] holds exactly when KeyFacts holds (both directions), so the list of 5 facts below is the whole open part and cannot be made shorter
left_as_hypothesis: KeyFacts.total: slot 1 (the total supply) is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a

owner_facts.source: the ten-token audit, finding USDD-9: facts about the deployed bytes that the auditor confirmed and that matter to an owner or a user. Each is per call; none is a statement about live chain state.
facts: USDD-9.a: mint(usr, wad) needs only wards[caller] == 1; a ward can mint any amount to any address. rely and deny need the same, so any ward can add wards or remove every other ward. Treat every ward key as full mint authority. The proofs do not say who the wards are on chain (no state was read): list the wards on chain.
USDD-9.b: burn(usr, wad) needs no ward: caller == usr, or allowance[usr][caller] >= wad; an allowance of 2^256-1 is never reduced.

USDD-9.c: permit is DAI style: allowed != 0 sets the allowance to 2^256-1, allowed == 0 sets it to 0; expiry 0 means no expiry; the nonce must equal nonces[holder]. The domain separator is the word of storage slot 5, fixed at construction and not rebuilt from CHAINID (no CHAINID opcode in the code), so a signature is valid on any chain fork that carries the same storage.

USDD-9.d: dirty inputs are accepted: address arguments are masked, 'allowed' is any nonzero word, v is masked to its low byte. The contract adds no check on s beyond the precompile's, so the mirrored signature (n - s, other v) also passes; the nonce stops a replay.
USDD-9.e: no zero address check in transfer, transferFrom, mint; tokens sent to address 0 stay in the sum.
USDD-9.f: every function reverts on value; no CALL, DELEGATECALL, SELFDESTRUCT or CREATE in the code; the only outside call is the STATICCALL to address 1.
